title: The site onboarding configuration an administrator reads and replaces
description: GET /api/v1/server/onboarding returns the configuration with its version; PUT replaces the whole document when expected_version is the current version (409 version_conflict otherwise) and returns the new configuration. Administrator, session and CSRF are required. Rejections are fixed codes shared with root's admin onboarding CLI: invalid_document, invalid_mode, invalid_repository_name, too_many_defaults, duplicate_default, duplicate_destination, unknown_provider, duplicate_provider, invalid_offer, site_key_unavailable (offer site_key without a stored key), site_key_stored (offer changed while one is stored). Integrations come back in the integrations catalog's order. A change applies only to onboardings that start afterwards. The site AI key has its own writes, each answered with the configuration: POST /api/v1/server/onboarding/ai-key/set {provider, key} stores it and makes offer site_key; POST /api/v1/server/onboarding/ai-key/delete {offer} removes it and sets that offer. Their rejections are invalid_key, invalid_offer and site_key_unavailable (nothing to delete); a 503 may or may not have written, and nothing is retried. The key is read back only as site_key {provider, suffix, set_at}; it is copied into a new person's own Pi credentials at the sign-in that created their account, never over a credential they have. People who joined earlier are given it by an administrator: GET /api/v1/server/onboarding/ai-key/copies lists joined people with the copy the site gave each (the site's own record, not what their Pi holds); POST …/ai-key/check {subject} asks that person's own daemon for one word about their Pi and writes nothing; POST …/ai-key/seed {subject, provider, suffix, set_at} has their daemon write the key under Pi's lock where the provider has no entry or exactly an earlier site copy, never over their own credential. Their rejections are subject_unavailable (404: not a joined, admitted person), site_key_unavailable, site_key_changed (409: the stored key is not the one named) and site_key_busy (409: another key change is running). A set that replaces a key also replaces every recorded copy of an earlier key of the same provider and answers each in rotation; a delete leaves copies with their people.

defaults.description: The site's default repositories; the same list in every mode. Never sent to a person's browser.

mode.description: preselected: the chooser starts with the defaults chosen; auto: the defaults are fetched right after GitHub sign-in; skip: no repository step, the defaults are imported in the background.

required.description: True removes the step's skip action; it gates no access.

offer.description: all: every option; one option: suggested first with the rest behind a link; site_key: exactly while the site holds an AI key, which skips the step.

version.description: Revision of the stored document; 0 until the first save.

rotation.description: Only in the reply of a set that replaced the site key: each person whose recorded copy was of an earlier key of the same provider, with their daemon's answer.

site_key.description: The stored site AI key as it is ever read back; present exactly while one is stored.

key.description: One literal key, sent once and never returned: Pi runs !… values and expands $NAME references. sk-ant-… exactly for anthropic.

offer.description: What new people are offered instead.

give_outcome.description: seeded: written where the provider had no entry; replaced: an earlier site copy replaced; already_current: holds this key; kept: the person's own credential, untouched; not_reached: nothing was sent; unknown: no answer, so it may or may not have written.

copy.description: The site key copy the site gave a person, from its own record.

suffix.description: The given key's last four characters.

current.description: The copy is of the key the site stores now.

people.description: Joined people who are not withdrawn, in the access list's order.

waiting.description: Allowed people who have not signed in yet; they get the key at their first sign-in.

state.description: What the person's Pi holds for the site key's provider: absent, exactly the current or an earlier site key, or own (anything else, a subscription included; its kind is never told); unknown when their daemon did not answer.

suffix.description: The stored key the administrator reviewed, as site_key names it.
